sections.h2: When to treat bindi and broadleaf weeds in Canberra
paras: Timing does most of the work. Bindi germinates through the cold months and is easiest to kill while small and soft, so the window is late winter to early spring, before it sets seed. Once you can feel prickles, next summer's seed is already in the lawn.

Clover, dandelion and capeweed respond well in spring and again in autumn, when they are growing actively. Hard frosts and hot, dry summer afternoons both reduce results, so we avoid spraying on frosty mornings, in strong wind or ahead of rain.
That is why bookings for weed spraying Canberra wide pick up from August. If you want bindi gone before summer, call in winter and we will schedule the first treatment for the right window.

We quote weed spraying Canberra jobs first, free and upfront, after seeing the yard or a few clear photos. On the day we check the weather, look over the lawn and beds, and treat the areas we agreed on. Keep pets and kids off treated areas until fully dry, and avoid mowing for a few days either side so the weeds have enough leaf to take the treatment in.
If you have regular mowing with us in Weston, Rivett, Evatt or elsewhere, the spraying can be built into the mowing schedule so the timing looks after itself.

sections.h2: Weed control and lawn health together
paras: Spraying removes the weeds, but it does not fill the gaps they leave. A thick lawn is the strongest long-term defence, so the weed spraying Canberra homeowners book in spring pairs well with regular mowing at the right height, plus fertilising and aeration through our lawn care service. Across Weston Creek, Woden Valley and Belconnen, a lawn cut regularly and kept dense into summer leaves weeds less room to take hold.

faqs.q: When should I spray for bindi if I want it gone before summer?
faqs.a: Late winter to early spring, before the bindi flowers and sets its spiky seed. For weed spraying Canberra wide that usually means August into September. Treating it early is far more effective than waiting until prickles appear, by which point next year's seed is already in the lawn.

faqs.q: How long do the kids and dog need to stay off the lawn?
faqs.a: Until the treated area is completely dry. Ask on the day, because drying time depends on temperature, wind and humidity. Hot spring afternoons dry quickly and cool, overcast mornings take longer. If in doubt, give it the rest of the day.

faqs.q: Do you do weed spraying Canberra wide, or only in Weston Creek?
faqs.a: We cover most of Canberra, including Kaleen and Evatt in Belconnen, Weston and Rivett in Weston Creek, Mawson and Pearce in Woden Valley, plus Queanbeyan across the border. Call us with your suburb and we will confirm.

faqs.q: Will spraying kill my lawn as well as the weeds?
faqs.a: No. On lawns we use selective treatments that target broadleaf weeds and bindi while leaving the grass. Kikuyu, couch, buffalo and fescue do not all tolerate the same products, which is why weed spraying Canberra lawns properly starts with identifying the grass.

faqs.q: Do I need more than one treatment?
faqs.a: Often one well-timed weed spraying Canberra visit handles bindi for the season. Heavy infestations, or beds and paths with a deep seed bank, may need a second pass a few weeks later. We tell you at the quote stage if that is likely.
